text:
alex: Heads-up: we saw a regression on the kernel handoff path when QPS spikes >1200/s in the synth harness. perf-bot reported ~12% p95 increase.
miriam: can you paste the CI log? which kernel switch path triggered it?
alex: here's the microtrace snippet we grabbed from the agent: 
```
[2026-03-15T12:03:21Z] kernel_select: chose fp16_int8_v2 for model-x, latency_est=8.2ms
[2026-03-15T12:03:22Z] handoff: fallback to fp16_generic (cold kv layout) cost +3.5ms
[2026-03-15T12:03:22Z] kv: miss for prefix=usr-req-3, reason=layout_mismatch
```
jon: did batching heuristics trigger a forced flush? our batch policy has max_wait_ms=5ms and max_batch_tokens=4096 right now.
alex: yes — forced flushes when queue depth hit ~1.3x expected during the ramp window. We saw small batches piling up and then a handoff happened mid-flight.
miriam: noisy KV cold miss rate? sam: KV warmup looks fine for steady QPS but during sawtooth ramps cold_ratio spikes from ~1% to 6-7%.
alex: replay harness used a custom wave ramp: 1m linear ramp 500->2000qps, sustain 30s, drop to 200, repeat. I can share the config if useful.
nina: suggestion: increase prefix caching TTL and avoid evictions during short bursts. Also try kernel probe flag --prefer-contiguous to reduce layout churn.
jon: can we run an apples-to-apples comparison: kernel-selection=dynamic vs kernel-selection=conservative with identical seeds and qps seed? perf-bot: queued job 7742/7743.
perf-bot: Job 7742 finished (dynamic): p50=22ms, p95=98ms, p99=245ms, kv_miss_rate=4.8%, avg_batch_size=3.1
perf-bot: Job 7743 finished (conservative): p50=24ms, p95=84ms, p99=190ms, kv_miss_rate=2.1%, avg_batch_size=2.8
miriam: interesting — conservative selection reduces tail at cost of slightly higher median. That points to batching vs kernel mismatch tradeoff, not pure throughput.
sam: hypothesis: kernel handoff causes temporary KV meta-layout mismatch -> transient miss spike because new kernel expects contiguous pages. Misses plus forced flush => tail.
alex: repro plan: instrument kv layout headers during kernel transitions and run spike replay with controlled warmup. I'll open a bench run and attach traces.
jon: also capture queueing depth histogram and exact flush timings. Use this command: 
```
benchctl run --profile=kv-meta --qps-pattern=sawtooth --seed=42 --duration=20m --corpus=v3.2
```
miriam: for apples-to-apples: same random seed, same corpus file, identical model weights and compile flags. Tag results with run_id and artifacts (traces, qps_{ramp}.csv).
nina: if regression reproduces, consider adding a deferred-handshake: when switching kernels, delay accepting new requests for a stable window (e.g., 100ms) while we ensure KV warm state. Could drop a small amount of throughput but smooth p95.
sam: agree — prototype as opt-in flag first (kernel_switch_stabilize_ms). Expect ~0.5-1% steady-state latency inflation but big p95 wins on spikes.
alex: ok i'll kick off probe runs (7744+) with debug-level kernel_select logs only to reduce noise and post perf diffs. Will also attach a small flamegraph and the kv_hit/miss time-series. :thumbsup:
jon: thanks. small ask: keep logs scoped to kernel_select+kv to avoid huge TCO.
alex: ack. I'll post artifacts here when the runs complete. If we confirm, we can add a short RFC for the deferred-handshake and run canary on dedicated clusters.
miriam: perfect — please also add a synthetic test that exercises ramp shapes: sawtooth, pulse, long-tail exponential so we have coverage across burst morphologies.
alex: noted. kickoff in 15m, will post links.
